Structure of Solids-Introduction
固体的结构-介绍

1. Introduction  1. 引言

An IC comprises millions of interconnected transistors, resistors, capacitors, etc.
一个集成电路由数百万个互连的晶体管、电阻器、电容器等组成。
Metals - used for interconnects, contacts, and in the transistor structure.
金属 - 用于互连、接触和晶体管结构中。
Examples: aluminium, copper, tungsten, polysilicon, metal silicides.
例子：铝、铜、钨、多晶硅、金属硅化物。
Dielectrics - for electrical insulation, mechanical support and environmental protection; part of device structure (transistor, capacitor dielectric). Examples: silicon dioxide, silicon nitride, various polymers.
电介质 - 用于电绝缘、机械支撑和环境保护；设备结构的一部分（晶体管、电容器电介质）。例子：二氧化硅、氮化硅、各种聚合物。
Semiconductors - used to make the active device (transistors, LEDs, lasers). Examples: silicon, germanium, GaAs.
半导体 - 用于制造主动器件（晶体管、LED、激光器）。例子：硅、锗、GaAs。

Pentium 4 microprocessor
奔腾 4 微处理器

1.3 Classes of semiconductors
1.3 半导体的类别

  • Elemental semiconductors
    元素半导体
Found in Group IV of periodic table. E.g. silicon (Si), germanium (Ge) Used in ICs and discrete devices such as transistors, diodes.
在周期表的第四组中发现。例如，硅（Si）、锗（Ge）用于集成电路和离散器件，如晶体管、二极管。
  • Compound semiconductors Compounds of Gp III & Gp V (III-V s/c e.g. GaAs, GaN, AlGaAs) Compounds of Gp II & Gp VI (II-VI s/c e.g. ZnS, CdTe, HgSe ) Used in light emitting devices such as LEDs and lasers.
    化合物半导体 Ⅲ族和Ⅴ族的化合物（Ⅲ-Ⅴ族半导体，例如 GaAs、GaN、AlGaAs） Ⅱ族和Ⅵ族的化合物（Ⅱ-Ⅵ族半导体，例如 ZnS、CdTe、HgSe） 用于发光设备，如 LED 和激光器。
  • Metal oxides  金属氧化物
Many metal oxides are also semiconductors (e.g. ZnO , SnO ZnO , SnO ZnO,SnO\mathrm{ZnO}, \mathrm{SnO} ). Used for gas and chemical sensing.
许多金属氧化物也是半导体（例如 ZnO , SnO ZnO , SnO ZnO,SnO\mathrm{ZnO}, \mathrm{SnO} ）。用于气体和化学传感。
  • Organic semiconductors  有机半导体
Long-chain polymers (e.g. poly-paraphenylen-vinylene PPV) Small molecules (e.g. pentacene) Used in OLED displays and polymer electronics.
长链聚合物（例如聚对苯撑乙烯 PPV）小分子（例如五烯）用于 OLED 显示器和聚合物电子产品。

  • Group III (B, AI, Ga, In) and Group V (P, As, Sb) elements used to “dope” Si.
    用于“掺杂”硅的第三组（B、AI、Ga、In）和第五组（P、As、Sb）元素。

2. Types of Solids
2. 固体的类型

Classification according to the size of the ordered region:
根据有序区域的大小进行分类：
  • Amorphous  无定形
Order in the range of a few atoms or on molecular dimensions
在几个原子或分子尺度的范围内下订单
  • Single-crystal  单晶
One large crystal making up entire volume of material.
一个大型晶体构成了整个材料的体积。
Regularity of atomic arrangement present throughout entire solid.
整个固体中存在原子排列的规律性。
  • Polycrystalline  多晶体
High degree of order over many atomic / molecular dimensions.
在许多原子/分子维度上具有高度的有序性。
Ordered single-crystal regions are called grains.
有序的单晶区域称为晶粒。
Grains vary in size and orientation. Grain
谷物在大小和方向上有所不同。谷物
Amorphous  无定形
Polycrystalline  多晶体
Single-crystal  单晶

Structure of Solids-Crystal Structure
固体的结构-晶体结构

3. Crystal Structure and Ordering:
3. 晶体结构与排序：

  • 3 phases or states of matter: Solid, Liquid and Gas
    物质的三种相或状态：固体、液体和气体
  • Gas state: Individual atoms independent of each other; atoms randomly fill a volume (No ordering).
    气体状态：个别原子彼此独立；原子随机填充一个体积（没有排序）。
  • Liquid state: Individual atoms somewhat free to move around. The hydrogen bond is a typical short range ordering.
    液态：个别原子在一定程度上可以自由移动。氢键是一种典型的短程有序。
  • Solid State  固态
    -Atoms in solids may be randomly positioned (as in a liquid) - Amorphous Solids (e.g. glasses) or
    - 固体中的原子可能随机排列（如在液体中） - 非晶固体（例如玻璃）或
  • Arranged in an orderly, repeating pattern within the material - Crystalline Solids (long range ordering)
    在材料中以有序、重复的模式排列 - 晶体固体（长程有序）
  • Polycrystals: grains are randomly oriented.
    多晶体：晶粒随机取向。

Structure of Solids-Crystal Structure
固体的结构-晶体结构

Crystalline Solids:  晶体固体：

The fact that one can alter the properties of semiconductors over a wide range may have something to do with the atomic arrangement of atoms in these materials. So, let us look at the crystal structure.
一个人可以在很大范围内改变半导体的性质，这可能与这些材料中原子的原子排列有关。那么，让我们来看看晶体结构。

(a) Amorphous  (a) 非晶态
No recognizable long-range order
没有可识别的长程有序性

(b) Polycrystalline  (b) 多晶体
Completely ordered in segments
完全按段落排序

© Crystalline
Entire solid is made up of atoms in an orderly array
整个固体是由有序排列的原子组成的
Figure 1.1  图 1.1

Example:  示例：

Amorphous Si thin film transistors used as switching devices in LCDs Polycrystalline Si used as gate in MOSFETs Actual active region of MOSFET is fabricated in crystalline Si
用于 LCD 的非晶硅薄膜晶体管作为开关器件 多晶硅用于 MOSFET 的栅极 MOSFET 的实际活跃区域是在晶体硅中制造的

Lattice and Basis:  晶格和基底：

Lattice: periodic array of points in space
晶格：空间中周期性排列的点阵
Basis: one atom or group of atoms attached to the lattice point
基底：一个原子或一组原子附着在晶格点上
The structure of all crystals can be described in terms of a lattice, with a group of atoms (basis) attached to every lattice point
所有晶体的结构可以用晶格来描述，每个晶格点上附有一组原子（基元）
The atomic arrangement determines the macro-properties of the crystal.
原子的排列决定了晶体的宏观性质。

Lattice + Basis = crystal structure

Lattice and Basis:  晶格和基底：

  • Lattice points are infinitesimal points in space.
    格点是空间中的无穷小点。
  • Atoms are physical objects
    原子是物理对象
  • Lattice points do not necessarily lie at the centre of atoms (slide 17)
    晶格点不一定位于原子的中心（幻灯片 17）
  • The number , composition, and arrangement of atoms is the same for each lattice point.
    每个晶格点的原子数量、组成和排列是相同的。

The 14 lattice types in three dimensions
三维中的 14 种晶格类型
There are 14 (only) Bravais Lattices:
有 14 种（仅）布拉维晶格：
There are only 14 unique ways to fill space with a periodic arrangement of points.
只有 14 种独特的方法可以用周期性排列的点填充空间。
Once you specify the lattice, you can then “decorate” your lattice with
一旦您指定了晶格，您就可以用来“装饰”您的晶格
a collection of atoms. Each lattice point must be decorated with the same collection of atoms.
一组原子。每个晶格点必须装饰有相同的原子集合。
Most elemental metals (about 90 %) crystallize into three densely packed crystal structures:
大多数元素金属（约 90%）结晶成三种密集堆积的晶体结构：
BCC (Fe, W, Mo, Nb, Ta, V, Cr), FCC (Cu, Al,Au, Ag, Pb , Ni, Pt) and HCP (Mg, Ti, Zn, Be, Co, Zr, Cd).
BCC (Fe, W, Mo, Nb, Ta, V, Cr), FCC (Cu, Al, Au, Ag, Pb, Ni, Pt) 和 HCP (Mg, Ti, Zn, Be, Co, Zr, Cd)。

Closed Packed Structures

Most efficient way of packing equal sized spheres.
最有效的相同大小球体打包方式。
In 2D, have close packed layers
在二维中，具有紧密堆积的层

Lattice and Basis:  晶格和基底：

3D Closed Packed Structures
3D 密堆积结构

Fig. 1-24  图 1-24
First layer is A (blue) and second layer is B (red).
第一层是 A（蓝色），第二层是 B（红色）。
Third layer, there are two possibilities:
第三层，有两种可能性：
(1) Can have A position again (blue). This leads to the regular sequence …ABABABA…Hexagonal close packing (hcp)
(1) 可以再次拥有 A 位置（蓝色）。这导致了规律序列 …ABABABA… 六方密堆积（hcp）
(2) Can have layer in C position (green), followed by the same repeat, to give …ABCABCABC… Cubic close packing (ccp)
(2) 可以在 C 位置（绿色）有层，后面跟着相同的重复，以给出……ABCABCABC……立方紧密堆积（ccp）

Atomic packing factor or packing density
原子堆积因子或堆积密度

Maximum fraction of the volume in a unit cell occupied by the atoms. Assume that the atoms are closely packed and that they can be treated as hard spheres. This fraction is called atomic packing factor (APF) or packing density.
单位晶胞中被原子占据的最大体积分数。假设原子是紧密堆积的，并且可以视为硬球。这个分数称为原子堆积因子（APF）或堆积密度。

APF = number of atoms per cell × volume of one atom volume of unit cell =  number of atoms per cell  ×  volume of one atom   volume of unit cell  =(" number of atoms per cell "xx" volume of one atom ")/(" volume of unit cell ")=\frac{\text { number of atoms per cell } \times \text { volume of one atom }}{\text { volume of unit cell }}

Crystal Direction and Surface Orientation

Example  示例

(A) Wafer flats are straight-line regions along the periphery of a wafer. The longer primary flat is positioned to facilitate identification of crystalline directions lying within the surface plane. The position of the shorter secondary flat relative to the primary flats indicates by inspection the wafer type ( n n nn or p p pp ) and the surface orientation [(100) or (111)].
(A) 晶圆平面是沿晶圆周边的直线区域。较长的主平面被放置以便于识别位于表面平面内的晶体方向。较短的次平面相对于主平面的定位通过检查指示晶圆类型（ n n nn 或 p p pp ）和表面取向[(100)或(111)]。
(B)Identification of the noted directions in the (100) and (111) surface planes allows the positioning of devices to achieve the maximum yield when dividing the wafer into segments (called die) containing individual devices. With the identification of one direction in the surface plane, it also becomes possible to deduce the orientation of any other direction in the surface plane. This is useful when optimal operating conditions require the special positioning of a pattern or device on the surface of the wafer.
(B)在(100)和(111)表面平面中识别出所述方向，可以在将晶圆分割成包含单个器件的段（称为芯片）时实现设备的最佳放置以获得最大产量。通过识别表面平面中的一个方向，也可以推导出表面平面中任何其他方向的取向。当最佳操作条件要求在晶圆表面上对图案或器件进行特殊定位时，这一点非常有用。

    主要键的特征是大的原子间力：1.离子键
    2.Covalent bond  2.共价键
    3.Metallic bond  3.金属键
  • Secondary bonds (Van der Waals forces) can be play an important role in solids, but they are generally much weaker
    次级键（范德瓦尔斯力）在固体中可以发挥重要作用，但它们通常要弱得多

Structure of Solids-Atomic Bonding
固体的结构-原子键合

4.1 Covalent Bonding  4.1 共价键

-Covalent bonds are formed when 2 atoms share a pair of electrons to form closed valence shells (of 8 electrons).
-共价键是在两个原子共享一对电子以形成封闭的价电子层（8 个电子）时形成的。
-Primary form of bonding between non-metallic elements, e.g., H 2 O , N 2 , CO 2 H 2 O , N 2 , CO 2 H_(2)O,N_(2),CO_(2)\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}, \mathrm{N}_{2}, \mathrm{CO}_{2}
-非金属元素之间的主要结合形式，例如， H 2 O , N 2 , CO 2 H 2 O , N 2 , CO 2 H_(2)O,N_(2),CO_(2)\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}, \mathrm{N}_{2}, \mathrm{CO}_{2}
-Group IV elements, e.g. Si, Ge, also tend to form covalent bonds. Each atom has 4 valence electrons which form 4 covalent bonds with 4 adjacent atoms. Results in a macromolecular solid.
-IV 族元素，例如 Si、Ge，也倾向于形成共价键。每个原子有 4 个价电子，与 4 个相邻原子形成 4 个共价键。形成宏观分子固体。

Structure of Solids-Atomic Bonding
固体的结构-原子键合

4.1 Covalent Bonding  4.1 共价键

-Characteristics of covalently bonded solids (macromolecules):
-共价键合固体（大分子）的特征：
∙ ∙ ∙\bullet Hard & strong with high melting points, e.g. 3815 ∘ C 3815 ∘ C 3815^(@)C3815^{\circ} \mathrm{C} for diamond, 1414 ∘ C 1414 ∘ C 1414^(@)C1414{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C} for silicon (strong bonds).
∙ ∙ ∙\bullet 硬且强，熔点高，例如 3815 ∘ C 3815 ∘ C 3815^(@)C3815^{\circ} \mathrm{C} 钻石， 1414 ∘ C 1414 ∘ C 1414^(@)C1414{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C} 硅（强键）。
-Brittle.  -脆弱。
-Electrically insulating at low temperatures (valence electrons are involved in covalent bonding). Silicon and germanium are semiconductors at room temperature
- 在低温下电绝缘（价电子参与共价键）。硅和锗在室温下是半导体。

Structure of Solids-Atomic Bonding
固体的结构-原子键合

4.2 Metallic Bonding  4.2 金属键合

-Simple metals have a valence shell with 1, 2 , or 3 electrons (e.g. Na, Ca, AI).
简单金属的价壳层有 1、2 或 3 个电子（例如：Na、Ca、AI）。
-In a solid metal, the valence electrons become delocalized, and each metal atom contributes its valence electrons to a common pool of electrons. Can be visualized as positive metallic ion cores (atoms without their valence electrons) in a “sea” of electrons.
在固体金属中，价电子变得去局域化，每个金属原子将其价电子贡献给一个共同的电子池。可以想象成在“电子海”中存在正的金属离子核心（没有价电子的原子）。
  • Solid is held together by electrostatic attraction between the +ve ion cores and the -ve sea of electrons.
    固体是通过正离子核心与负电子海之间的静电吸引力结合在一起的。
    -Mobile “free” electrons give rise to good electrical & thermal conduction.
    -移动的“自由”电子导致良好的电导率和热导率。
Sodium Atom  钠原子
Sodium Solid  钠固体

Structure of Solids-Crystalline Imperfection
固体结构-晶体缺陷

5. Crystalline Imperfections
5. 晶体缺陷

The ideal single-crystal structure has every atom positioned regularly in the crystal lattice. A real crystal is not perfect, and these imperfections alter the electrical properties of the material.
理想的单晶结构中，每个原子在晶格中都规则地排列。真实的晶体并不完美，这些缺陷改变了材料的电气性质。

5.1 Lattice Vibrations  5.1 晶格振动

-Atoms vibrate around their lattice sites due to thermal energy.
-原子由于热能在其晶格位置周围振动。
-As atoms are bonded together, these vibrations are collective and propagate throughout the crystal lattice as phonons.
-当原子结合在一起时，这些振动是集体的，并作为声子在晶格中传播。
-Lattice vibrations disrupt the otherwise perfect geometric arrangement of atoms. -Cause the scattering of charge carriers, e.g. electrons, through the crystal.
-晶格振动破坏了原本完美的原子几何排列。 -导致电荷载流子（例如电子）在晶体中散射。
-Greater scattering at higher temperatures.
-在更高温度下散射更强。
Electron scattering by lattice vibration
晶格振动引起的电子散射

Structure of Solids-Crystalline Imperfection
固体结构-晶体缺陷

5. Crystalline Imperfections
5. 晶体缺陷

5.2 Point Defects  5.2 点缺陷

-Zero-dimensional (point) defects in the crystal:
-零维（点）缺陷在晶体中：
-Vacancy - a missing atom.
-空位 - 一个缺失的原子。
-Interstitial - atom located between lattice sites.
-间隙 - 位于晶格位置之间的原子。
-Distorts the lattice and destroys the perfect geometric arrangement of atoms.
-扭曲晶格，破坏原子完美的几何排列。
-Bonding between atoms also disrupted, and changes the electrical properties of the material.
原子之间的结合也被破坏，并改变了材料的电气特性。
-Point defects can scatter charge carriers.
点缺陷可以散射电荷载流子。
Electron scattering by lattice vibration
晶格振动引起的电子散射

Structure of Solids-Crystalline Imperfection
固体结构-晶体缺陷

5. Crystalline Imperfections
5. 晶体缺陷

5.3 Dislocations  5.3 位错

-One-dimensional (line) defects in the crystal, e.g. missing row of atoms.
晶体中的一维（线）缺陷，例如缺失的原子行。
-Disrupts the normal geometric periodicity of the lattice.
-破坏了晶格的正常几何周期性。
-Disrupts the bonding between atoms in the crystal.
-破坏晶体中原子之间的结合。
-Effects are more severe than point defects as they are of a larger extent than a single point.
- 效果比点缺陷更严重，因为它们的范围大于单个点。

Structure of Solids-Crystalline Imperfection
固体结构-晶体缺陷

5. Crystalline Imperfections
5. 晶体缺陷

5.3 Grain Boundaries  5.3 粒界

-Considered as two-dimensional (surface) defects.
-被视为二维（表面）缺陷。
-Individual grains (small reasonably perfect crystals) terminate on grain boundaries, where alignment of crystal planes between adjacent grains is interrupted.
- 单个晶粒（小而相对完美的晶体）在晶界处终止，邻近晶粒之间的晶面对齐被打断。
-Grain boundaries contain voids, stretched & broken bonds, and misplaced atoms.
- grain boundaries 包含空洞、拉伸和断裂的键以及错位的原子。
  • Carrier scattering is unavoidable at grain boundaries.
    载流子散射在晶界处是不可避免的。
Polysilicon  多晶硅
Polycrystalline diamond  多晶金刚石

Structure of Solids-Crystalline Imperfection
固体结构-晶体缺陷

5. Crystalline Imperfections
5. 晶体缺陷

5.4 Impact of lattice defects on electrical properties
5.4 晶格缺陷对电学性质的影响

-In a perfect crystal with no lattice scattering, charge carriers can travel through the crystal without resistance.
在没有晶格散射的完美晶体中，电荷载流子可以无阻力地穿过晶体。
-Conversely, the greater the extent of the imperfection in the crystal lattice, the greater the scattering.
相反，晶格中缺陷的程度越大，散射就越大。
  • Hence a grain boundary is a more extensive scatterer than a dislocation, which in turn is worse than a point defect.
    因此，晶界是比位错更广泛的散射体，而位错又比点缺陷更差。

Structure of Solids-Crystalline Imperfection
固体结构-晶体缺陷

5. Crystalline Imperfections
5. 晶体缺陷

5.4 Impact of lattice defects on electrical properties
5.4 晶格缺陷对电学性质的影响

Example: Copper  示例：铜

-Polycrystalline metals with large grains have lower resistivity.
-大晶粒的多晶金属具有较低的电阻率。
Electron scattering at grain boundaries
晶界处的电子散射

Structure of Solids-Crystalline Imperfection
固体结构-晶体缺陷

5.4 Impact of lattice defects on electrical properties
5.4 晶格缺陷对电学性质的影响

-In semiconductors, the grain size has a huge impact on the device performance.
在半导体中，晶粒大小对器件性能有很大影响。
-High-performance devices are made in single-crystal material (e.g. for logic ICs such as microprocessors).
高性能设备是由单晶材料制成的（例如，用于逻辑集成电路，如微处理器）。
-Polycrystalline semiconductors can only yield low-performance devices where cost is the overriding consideration (e.g. thin-film transistors in LCD displays).
多晶半导体只能生产低性能的器件，成本是主要考虑因素（例如，LCD 显示器中的薄膜晶体管）。
-One important parameter of a semiconductor is the carrier mobility - a measure of how mobile a charge carrier is in the material - the higher the better.
半导体的一个重要参数是载流子迁移率——衡量电荷载流子在材料中移动能力的指标——越高越好。
Condition of silicon  硅的状态

Structure of Solids-Crystalline Imperfection
固体结构-晶体缺陷

5. Crystalline Imperfections
5. 晶体缺陷

5.5 Impurities  5.5 杂质

-Foreign atoms in a crystal lattice.
-晶格中的外来原子。
-If they are located at normal lattice sites, they are substitutional impurities (i.e., they substitute for the host lattice atom).
如果它们位于正常晶格位置，则它们是替代杂质（即，它们替代宿主晶格原子）。
-If they are located between normal sites, they are interstitial impurities (i.e., they occupy interstitial sites).
如果它们位于正常位置之间，则它们是间隙杂质（即，它们占据间隙位置）。
  • In semiconductors, impurity atoms can be inert (e.g., carbon, oxygen), or they can drastically alter the electrical behaviour (e.g., gold, phosphorus).
    在半导体中，杂质原子可以是惰性的（例如，碳、氧），或者它们可以显著改变电气行为（例如，金、磷）。
    -Group III and V elements are used to dope silicon. To be electrically active, these dopants must occupy substitutional sites, and form covalent bonds with the silicon.
    -III 组和 V 组元素用于掺杂硅。为了具有电活性，这些掺杂剂必须占据替代位点，并与硅形成共价键。

Structure of Solids-Growth of Semiconductor Materials
固体的结构-半导体材料的生长

6. Growth of Semiconductor Materials
6. 半导体材料的增长

-Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI) ICs are fabricated on single-crystal silicon.
超大规模集成 (VLSI) 集成电路在单晶硅上制造。
-The starting “wafer” is cut from a single-crystal of silicon. Typical wafer diameter in current production are 300 and 450 mm . In the 1970s, Si wafers were typically 75 mm in diameter.
-起始的“晶圆”是从单晶硅中切割而成。目前生产中典型的晶圆直径为 300 和 450 毫米。在 1970 年代，硅晶圆的直径通常为 75 毫米。
300 mm wafer  300 毫米晶圆

Structure of Solids-Growth of Semiconductor Materials
固体的结构-半导体材料的生长

6.1 Growing a single crystal
6.1 生长单晶

-In nature, most solids are polycrystalline. Large singlecrystals are rare. Why?
在自然界中，大多数固体是多晶体。大单晶体很少见。为什么？
-Consider growth from a molten (or liquid) state. The process of solidification first starts off with the formation of small clusters of atoms known as nuclei at or just below the freezing point.
-考虑从熔融（或液态）状态的生长。固化过程首先从在冰点或略低于冰点的地方形成称为核的小原子簇开始。
-The nuclei grow by the addition of atoms from the liquid phase.
- 核心通过从液相中添加原子而生长。
-At the end of the solidification process, the grains abut each other at
-在固化过程结束时，晶粒相互接触于
random orientations, resulting in a polycrystalline solid.
随机取向，形成多晶固体。

Structure of Solids-Growth of Semiconductor Materials
固体的结构-半导体材料的生长

6.2 Growth of silicon crystal using
6.2 硅晶体的生长使用

Czochralski (CZ) method  Czochralski (CZ) 方法

-Start with purified polysilicon chips in a crystal pulling furnace, & melted (m.p. = 1410 ∘ C 1410 ∘ C 1410^(@)C1410^{\circ} \mathrm{C} ). Desired impurities (dopants) added to melt to control the electrical characteristics of the grown crystal.
-从晶体拉伸炉中的纯化多晶硅芯片开始，熔化（熔点 = 1410 ∘ C 1410 ∘ C 1410^(@)C1410^{\circ} \mathrm{C} ）。将所需的杂质（掺杂剂）添加到熔体中，以控制生长晶体的电气特性。
-Tiny seed crystal (single-crystal of desired crystal orientation, low defect density) is brought into contact with the surface of the melt.
-微小种晶（具有所需晶体取向的单晶，低缺陷密度）与熔体表面接触。
  • Seed crystal is withdrawn slowly as it is rotated.
    种晶体在旋转时缓慢抽出。
    -Liquid solidifies onto the seed crystal as it is pulled. Size of crystal depends on pull rate.
    液体在被拉动时固化到种晶上。晶体的大小取决于拉动速度。

Structure of Solids-Growth of Semiconductor Materials
固体的结构-半导体材料的生长

-Ingot is sliced up into wafers
-锭被切割成薄片
∼ 1 mm ∼ 1 mm ∼1mm\sim 1 \mathrm{~mm} thick.   ∼ 1 mm ∼ 1 mm ∼1mm\sim 1 \mathrm{~mm} 厚。
-Wafers are then lapped & polished.
- 然后对晶圆进行磨光和抛光。
ID Water Sicing Sow  ID 水切割播种
Wafer Polishing  晶圆抛光
